title: CmdPal: Qualify fallback identity and ranking by provider

proposed_comments.body:
**Severity: Medium — disabled fallback commands can still contribute global results.**

`MainListPage` adds items satisfying this property to `specialFallbacks` before its `else if (s.IsEnabled)` check. Checking only the global-results flag therefore bypasses the fallback's enabled setting. The previous global-selection helper required both flags.

**If left unchanged:** a fallback saved with `IsEnabled=false` and `IncludeInGlobalResults=true` can continue producing global results despite being disabled.

```suggestion
    internal bool IncludeInGlobalResults => GetFallbackSettings() is { IsEnabled: true, IncludeInGlobalResults: true };
```

The four enabled/global combinations were exercised against the current source: only disabled/global=true fails before this replacement, and all four pass after it. The literal replacement compiles with analyzers enabled. This does not claim an interactive Command Palette run.

**Latest maintainer context:** The maintainer identifies a bad merge and says this wrapper had already been removed from main. Reconcile that merge first and do not restore retired code just to apply this draft. The observed enabled/global and reflection-input failures describe the still-present current revision; after removing or replacing that code, recheck the equivalent current path and retire any suggestion whose target disappears.
proposed_comments.title: Keep disabled fallbacks out of global results

confidence.rationale: The disabled/global=true regression fails on the exact current predicate, passes with the literal replacement, and the global-selection caller bypasses its enabled check for this branch.

proposed_comments.body:
**Severity: Medium — the ranking regression test currently fails before testing ranking.**

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Tests/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels.UnitTests/ProviderFallbackSettingsTests.cs`, `FallbackRanking_PrefersProviderQualifiedIdAndPreservesLegacyRank`; and the existing `MainListPage.ScoreFallbackItem` signature in `Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/Commands/MainListPage.cs`.

**Problem:** `ScoreFallbackItem` now accepts `InProcObject<IListItem>`, but all three reflection invocations still pass a raw `TopLevelFallbackViewModel`. Running this exact test throws `ArgumentException` because reflection cannot convert the argument to the wrapper type.

**Why it matters:** If left unchanged, the focused suite fails and none of these assertions verifies provider-qualified ranking or the legacy-rank fallback. This is a test failure, not a demonstrated production crash.

**Suggested change:**
1. Add the `Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels.Models` import to the test file.
2. Wrap each of the three reflection invocations' first arguments in `new InProcObject<IListItem>(...)`, retaining the existing ranks and expected scores.
3. Keep the production signature and all assertions; do not remove coverage merely to bypass the mismatch.

**Verification:** Run `ProviderFallbackSettingsTests`. The unmodified invocation fails on the current revision; repairing the three arguments removes that failure. Together with the separate enabled-fallback correction and four added enabled/global control cases, all 12 focused cases pass. This current revision also fixes the earlier formatting diagnostics: the exact test project and the minimal candidate both build with analyzers enabled.

**Latest maintainer context:** The maintainer identifies a bad merge and says this wrapper had already been removed from main. Reconcile that merge first and do not restore retired code just to apply this draft. The observed enabled/global and reflection-input failures describe the still-present current revision; after removing or replacing that code, recheck the equivalent current path and retire any suggestion whose target disappears.
proposed_comments.title: Pass the current wrapper type to the ranking regression test

confidence.rationale: The exact current test throws ArgumentException before its assertions; wrapping all three arguments compiles and the full twelve-case focused suite passes.

proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: This is a separate test repair coordinating its import and three invocation arguments; the enabled-fallback suggestion is independently applicable.
